history.period: 7th-8th century origins; present masonry structure 9th century Chola (per some sources - verify); expanded 11th century under the Cholas; later Vijayanagara additions; renovated 1903 and the 1970s
history.summary: An ancient seaside Shiva temple in Thiruvanmiyur, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams glorified by the 7th-century Saivite saints Appar (Thirunavukkarasar) and Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram; Arunagirinathar also composed hymns here. 'Marundu' means medicine in Tamil - Marundeeswarar is Shiva as the physician who taught sage Agastya the curative properties of herbs, so the temple has long been a place of healing worship for the ailing. Legend holds that sage Valmiki worshipped Shiva here to be absolved of his robber past, and the place was called Thiruvalmikiyur, which became Thiruvanmiyur; a Valmiki shrine stands on the temple's western side by the East Coast Road (spared from road-widening demolition by a Madras High Court directive). The road from the temple, called Vadagaperuvazhi in Chola times, linked the Chola kingdom to Thanjavur and Andhra; inscriptions in the Tripurasundari Amman shrine date to Rajendra Chola's 11th-century reign. Along with Kapaleeshwarar and Thiruvottriyur Thyagarajaswami, it forms the celebrated Trinity Sea Shore Temples of Thondai Mandalam (verify). Covers about 1 acre with two gateway towers and a large temple tank; the five sacred ponds are Janmanasini, Kamanasini, Papanasini, Gnanadhayini and Mokshadhayini. Sources conflict on gopuram tiers (seven-tiered per some, five-tiered per others - verify). Six daily rituals are performed. Maintained by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department; latest kumbhabhishekam February 2020 (previous May 2008 - weakly sourced, verify).

name: Marundeeswarar Temple
town_description: Thiruvanmiyur is a coastal neighbourhood in south Chennai on the East Coast Road, stretching from the Adyar river mouth toward the Bay of Bengal. It blends an old temple-town core around the Marundeeswarar temple with modern residential blocks and the Thiruvanmiyur bus terminus and MRTS station nearby.

travel.railway: Thiruvanmiyur MRTS station - about 3 km (verify); Chennai Central about 15 km (verify).
travel.road: On the East Coast Road (ECR) at Thiruvanmiyur, Chennai 600041; two entrances - one from ECR, one on West Tank Street. City buses stop at the nearby Thiruvanmiyur bus terminus.

visitor_information.best_time: November-February (cooler months); Panguni (March-April) for the Brahmotsavam.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00 PM-8:30 PM (some sources report morning opening at 5:30 AM and evening close at 9:00 PM - verify). No entry fee.
